deep.reconstruction:
PART A – 'Berechnung von Πi': Gauss computes Π(i) = Γ(1+i) (his Π(z) = Γ(z+1)) to 7 figures.

Step 1 (recursion downward). Π(i) = Π(10+i) / ∏_{k=1}^{10}(k+i). For each factor he tabulates log10|k+i| = ½ log10(k²+1) and arg(k+i) = arctan(1/k) in degrees, minutes and seconds. Rows: 1+i: 0.1505150, 45°0'0"; 2+i: 0.3494850, 26°33'54.187"; … ; 10+i: 1.0021607, 5°42'38.136". The sums are Σ log10|k+i| = 6.8218213 and Σ arg = 152°6'51.747".

Step 2 (Stirling series with complex argument n = 10+i). He uses log Π(n) = (n+½) log n − n + ½ log 2π + 1/(12n) − 1/(360n³) + …. Every complex log is kept as a pair: (Briggs log of the modulus, argument in sexagesimal). Natural-log quantities are converted with M = log10 e = 0.4342945, and radians with 206264.8".
- 10.5·log(10+i) gives 10.5·1.0021607 = 10.5226872 and argument 10.5·5°42'38.136" = 59°57'40.428".
- i·log(10+i) = i·ln|n| − θ, where θ = arctan 0.1 = 0.0996687 rad. This gives a modulus contribution −θM = −0.0432856 and an argument contribution ln√101 = 2.3075726 rad = 132°12'48.460".
- Subtotal: 10.4794016 and 192°10'28.888".
- The term −n = −(10+i), 'verw.' (converted), gives −10M = −4.3429448 and −1 rad = −57°17'44.806".
- Result so far: 6.1364568 and 134°52'44.082".

Step 3 (remaining terms, right column, 'Contr.' struck through). ½ ln 2π = 0.9189385. With 1/(12n) = (10−i)/1212 = 0.0082508 − 0.0008251i and −1/(360n³) = −0.0000026 + 0.0000008i, the sum is 0.9271867 − 0.0008243i (natural log).
- Conversion of the real part: log 0.9271867 = 9.9671672 (−10), plus log M = 9.6377843, giving 0.4026720 in Briggs units.
- Conversion of the imaginary part: log 0.0008243 = 6.91609 (−10); subtracting log(1" in radians) complement 4.68557 gives log 170.03" = 2'50.028".
- 'Die übrigen Glieder' therefore contribute +0.4026720 and −2'50.028".
- Total: log10|Π(10+i)| = 6.5391288 and arg = 134°49'54.054".

Step 4 (division). log10|Πi| = 6.5391288 − 6.8218213 = 9.7173075 (−10). arg Πi = 134°49'54.054" − 152°6'51.747" = −17°16'57.693".
- log cos of this angle = 9.9799354 and log sin = 9.4728829 (negative).
- Hence Πi = +0.4980156 − 0.1549496i.

Step 5 (independent control of the modulus). Πi·Π(−i) = πi/sin(πi) = π/sinh π = 2π e^{−π}/(1−e^{−2π}).
- log 2π = 0.7981799 and log e^π = πM = 1.3643764, difference 9.4338035.
- Complement of log(1−e^{−2π}) = 0.0008118 (Gauss writes 'Cp. 1−e^{2π}').
- Sum 9.4346153 (manuscript digit overwritten, read as …173). Half of this is 9.7173076, against 9.7173075 from Steps 1–4. The check succeeds.

PART B – fractional iteration (functional square roots).
(i) 'sin^{1/2} x' denotes the half-iterate φ with φ(φ(x)) = sin x, as a formal odd series: φ = x − x³/12 − x⁵/160 − 53x⁷/40320 − …. (My reconstruction:) put φ = x + a x³ + b x⁵ + c x⁷. Then φ∘φ = x + 2a x³ + (2b+3a²)x⁵ + (2c+8ab+3a³)x⁷. Matching with sin gives a = −1/12, b = −1/160, c = −53/40320.
(ii) He squares it: φ² = x² − x⁴/6 − x⁶/180 − x⁸/630.
(iii) With f(x) = e^x − 1 he gives the half-iterate f^{1/2}(x) = x + x²/4 + x³/48 + 0·x⁴ (the dot marks a vanishing term) + x⁵/3840 − x⁶/23040. Coefficients are fixed successively by matching f^{1/2}∘f^{1/2} with e^x − 1: 2a₂ = 1/2; 2a₃+2a₂² = 1/6; 2a₄+5a₂a₃+a₂³ = 1/24 ⇒ a₄ = 0; 2a₅+a₂a₃/2+a₃/4 = 1/120 ⇒ a₅ = 1/3840; …
errors: Coefficient of x⁶ in the half-iterate of e^x−1 is wrong: matching x⁶ gives 2a₆ + 142/92160 = 1/720 = 128/92160, so a₆ = −7/92160, not −1/23040 (= −4/92160). All earlier coefficients 1, 1/4, 1/48, 0, 1/3840 are correct.
Final imaginary part −0.1549496 should be −0.1549498 (true Γ(1+i) = 0.4980156681 − 0.1549498283i). This is accumulated 7-place-log rounding, not a method error. The real part 0.4980156 is correct.
'Cp. 1−e^{2π}' should read 1−e^{−2π}; the numerical value 0.0008118 is that of −log10(1−e^{−2π}), so this is a notational slip only.

The control-column line reads like 9.4346173, but 9.4338035 + 0.0008118 = 9.4346153. The halved value 9.7173076 written below corresponds to 9.4346153, so it is either an overwritten digit or a misreading.
All other logarithms, angles, the Stirling terms and the three sine half-iterate coefficients check correctly, as does the squared series.

deep.surprise_reason: The Γ(1+i) computation is a careful but routine application of Gauss's own Π-function theory (1812). The bottom of the page is more interesting: it shows Gauss explicitly computing functional square roots (half-iterates) of sin x and e^x−1 as power series, writing sin^{1/2} and f^{1/2}. These are the series now associated with Schröder/Koenigs-era fractional iteration and with mid-20th-century work by Baker, Erdős–Jabotinsky and Écalle. Babbage had treated functional roots around 1815, but explicit coefficient calculations like these are not generally attributed to Gauss. This is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major theorem: the computation is elementary coefficient matching, with no convergence analysis, and contains one error.

transcription_corrections: Right column: '9.4346173' should be 9.4346153 (= 9.4338035 + 0.0008118; the next line 9.7173076 is its half); the digit appears overwritten.
'Cp. 1−e^{2π}' is Gauss's shorthand for the complement of log(1−e^{−2π}).
'[-+-] − 0.0008251 i' in the 1/(12n) line: the sign is a corrected minus, i.e. 1/(12n) = +0.0082508 − 0.0008251 i.
'Contr[?]' at the top right is a struck-through 'Contr.' (Controle) heading, not part of the computation.
'10+i verw.' = the term −(10+i) converted (verwandelt) into Briggs log / arc units: −10M = −4.3429448 and −1 radian = −57°17'44.806".
Middle right lines '9.9671672 6,91609 / + 9.6377843 − 4.68557' are the log-conversions: log 0.9271867 + log M, and log 0.0008243 − log(arc 1") giving 170.03" = 2'50.03".
'sin^{1/2} x' and 'f^{1/2} x' denote half-iterates (functional square roots), not powers or inverse functions.
